message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Details | |-------|------------|---------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural interstate: 70 mph (except 55 mph on I‑35).
• Urban interstate: 65 mph.
• Residential streets: 25–35 mph (often 25 mph). | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001–545.004 | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers and drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.051–545.055 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed but drivers must remain attentive. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.041 | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Yield” signs require slowing and yielding to traffic already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.011–545.015 | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 20 mph during school hours (usually 7 a.m.–9 p.m.) unless posted otherwise.
• Speed limit may be lower during peak school times. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.013 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied or the vehicle is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.014 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or intersection.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited unless marked. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.020 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered and display valid license plates.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection (except exempt categories). | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001–545.002 | | **Commercial Vehicle Rules** | • Additional weight limits, licensing requirements, and safety inspections apply.
• Hours‑of‑Service regulations for truck drivers. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.050–545.055 | | **Emergency Vehicle Exemptions** | • Emergency vehicles with flashing lights may exceed speed limits and ignore certain traffic signals when responding to emergencies. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.030 | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Official rules, forms, and updates. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Statutory text available online. - **Local County Ordinances** – May impose additional restrictions (e.g., stricter school‑zone limits). --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for local road conditions. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check your mirrors** before changing lanes or turning. 4. **Keep a safe following distance** – especially on highways where speeds are higher. 5. **Be extra cautious in school zones** – speeds drop significantly and pedestrians are present. Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed information on a specific area (e.g., DUI penalties, commercial driving regulations, or recent legislative changes).
